sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: TIRF assay confirmed surface expression of V5-tagged IL-17RC on HEK-293T cells; functional signaling not explicitly measured for the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: The paper places the V5 tag 'at the N terminus' of full-length IL-17RC but names no specific residue. The signal peptide spans residues 1–20 (computed landmarks), so any N-terminal tag must be inserted after residue 20 to avoid being cleaved with the signal peptide; residue 21 (L) is the mature N-terminus and the first extracellular residue. This is the sole extracellular N-terminal junction, making the position topology-derived. TIRF on transfected HEK-293T cells confirmed surface display of the tagged protein. Full-length IL-17RC with V5 tag at the N-terminus expressed in HEK-293T cells; TIRF assay used to detect surface-displayed tagged protein (WT and truncation mutants Q138*, R376*, R378*). Paper states tag is 'at the N terminus' with no residue number.

sources.claim: The TIRF assay was performed on the transfected HEK-293T cells as described in “Cell purification and culture.” V5 tag–IL-17RC WT and mutant (Q138*, R376*, and R378*) vectors were constructed at the N terminus by the pcDNA3.1 Directional TOPO Expression kit (Life Technologies).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are from the same paper (PMC4419340) and describe the same V5-tagged IL-17RC construct; L1 is used as the primary supporting clip. L3 (PMC12961907) reports a C-terminal TEV protease fusion to full-length IL-17RC; the C-terminus (residue 791) falls within the intracellular domain (residues 560–791 per computed landmarks) and is therefore not a surface tag site — recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an internal extracellular loop insertion for IL-17RC.

literature_other_positions.note: Full-length IL-17RC fused to TEV protease at its C-terminus; residue 791 is the last intracellular residue (topology: 560–791 intracellular), so this fusion is cytoplasmic and not a surface tag site.
